niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why Beginners Feel Like Experts
ideas.angle: This video explains the Dunning-Kruger effect through the 'Peak of Mount Ignorant,' showing why people with the least knowledge often have the most confidence while experts doubt themselves.

hook.en: Why are the least talented people so confident?
hook.fr: Pourquoi les moins doués sont-ils si confiants ?

ideas.reason: Educational 'aha' moments about social frustrations perform well; the Dunning-Kruger effect currently sees high search volume on TikTok and Reels as people seek to explain online behavior.
sources: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology (Kruger & Dunning, 1999)

ideas.title: Why Having Options Makes You Miserable
ideas.angle: The Paradox of Choice reveals that more options lead to less satisfaction and higher anxiety. It explains why you can't pick a movie on Netflix or a meal at a restaurant.

hook.en: Too many choices are ruining your happiness.
hook.fr: Trop de choix gâchent ton bonheur.

ideas.reason: Universal relatability regarding digital era 'overload.' Shorts focusing on daily frustrations like 'scrolling forever' see high retention rates due to instant recognition.
sources: Barry Schwartz: The Paradox of Choice

ideas.title: Your Hidden Sixth Sense
ideas.angle: Most people think we only have five senses, but Proprioception—your brain's ability to know where your limbs are without looking—is what actually stops you from falling over.

hook.en: You actually have a sixth sense.
hook.fr: Tu as en réalité un sixième sens.

ideas.reason: The 'fact-check' style hook (debunking the 5-senses myth) creates a curiosity gap. Biology-based psychology facts have a high 'shareability' factor on mobile platforms.
sources: Harvard Medical School: The Science of Proprioception
